title: POC weekly sync - quantization INT8/FP8
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quantization experiment results on Atlas Health's LLM workloads. Team reviewed INT8 and FP8 deltas, discussed prompt-level quality regressions, kernel/hardware tuning, and next steps (additional evals, longer-run benchmarks on Dedicated, and a checklist for security docs).
action_items: Marco Ruiz - run 24h throughput run on Dedicated GPUs with FP8 profile, capture p95 latency and token/sec - due 2026-07-14
Priya Sethi - collect 200 more high-priority prompts that hit hallucination cases and share as CSV - due 2026-07-10
Lena Park - share updated benchmark sheet and pricing estimate for Dedicated burst capacity - due 2026-07-09
Aisha Khan - send SOC2/HIPAA packaging docs and KMS integration note - due 2026-07-08
next_steps: SE to run longer Dedicated perf run with FP8 and INT8 for 24 hours
Customer to provide extra failure/hallucination prompts
Redwood to produce updated cost/latency spreadsheet and suggested rollout plan (canary + fallback)
Schedule security follow-up for VPC/KMS questions week of 2026-07-13
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this to 45 mins. quick roll call?
[00:06] Daniel Cho: Daniel here.
[00:08] Priya Sethi: Priya on the line.
[00:09] Marta Gomez: Marta, hi.
[00:11] Marco Ruiz: Marco from Redwood here.
[00:13] Aisha Khan: Aisha from CSM.
[00:18] Lena Park: Great. Quick agenda — results recap for the INT8/FP8 runs, quality-impact review, tuning notes, and then next steps. Marco, you want to start with the numbers?
[00:28] Marco Ruiz: Sure. So we ran the three configs you asked: baseline FP16, INT8 quant, and FP8 quant on the same model checkpoint you provided. The short story: INT8 gives about 1.8x token/sec improvement vs FP16 but we saw a 3-6% drop on ROUGE/BLEU-style metrics on the long-form summarization set. FP8 sits in between: roughly 1.4x speedup and only about 1-2% metric delta.
[00:55] Priya Sethi: When you say ROUGE, that was on the 1k eval prompts we shared earlier?
[00:59] Marco Ruiz: Yes, exactly — the clinical summarization set with longer contexts. Also we instrumented soft-fail cases where the model hallucinated entities; INT8 had a slightly higher incidence, FP8 was close to FP16 in that dimension.
[01:13] Marta Gomez: That aligns with what we feared, the medical entity hallucinations are the high-risk item for us. 3-6% sounds small but in production it matters.
[01:21] Lena Park: Right. To be clear, the absolute numbers: INT8 produced a 4.8% drop on average on the top-1 precision for named entities, FP8 was 1.3% drop. Overall latency improvements were significant though — INT8 cut median latency by ~30% on your infra.
[01:39] Daniel Cho: Is that median or p95? We care about p95 for user-facing flows.
[01:42] Marco Ruiz: Good call — median was 30% but p95 saw about 18% improvement with INT8. FP8 p95 improved by 10-12%. Token throughput increased more noticeably in batch runs — about 2x for INT8 at 8k batching across the bench rig. Note: real production traffic shape will modify those numbers.
[02:02] Priya Sethi: Can you remind us which hardware you ran on? I think we gave you Ampere-class and a small A100 rack?
[02:09] Marco Ruiz: We ran the initial experiments on A100 40GBs and a couple of H100 dev nodes. INT8 on H100 gave slightly better fidelity than on A100 because of kernel and quant backend differences. There may be AVX/FP8 kernel differences across vendors; we noted that in the sheet.
[02:26] Daniel Cho: So practical recommendation — is FP8 the sweet spot for us?
[02:29] Marco Ruiz: For your use-case — long clinical summaries with high-accuracy entity extraction — FP8 seems like a safer tradeoff. INT8 gives better cost but requires more aggressive guardrails: prompt-level checks, rerankers, or bias-correction steps.
[02:41] Marta Gomez: Could we do INT8 for lower-risk flows and FP8 for high-risk?
[02:45] Lena Park: Yep, that's exactly a common rollout pattern — canary INT8 on non-sensitive routes, and FP8 or FP16 for protected flows with automatic fallback if confidence drops. We can configure routing rules in Redwood by route/model tag to do that.
[02:58] Priya Sethi: The hallucination cases — do you have examples from the run?
[03:02] Marco Ruiz: We captured 42 prompts that had entity hallucinations in INT8 that didn't appear in FP16. I can attach the sample CSV in the updated benchmark sheet.
[03:10] Lena Park: (link shared) benchmark sheet: https://redwood/sheets/atlas-quant-bench.xlsx - we'll drop the sample CSV in the 'hallucination-cases' tab.
[03:20] Speaker 1: Sorry can I ask a quick question about KV cache — is the caching behavior consistent across quant levels?
[03:25] Marco Ruiz: Good question. Yes, KV cache mechanics are the same, but quantization can slightly change activation ranges which can influence cache effectiveness for prefix reuse. We measured a tiny decrease in cache hit-rate in INT8 for very long prefix reuse cases, probably due to numeric drift.
[03:40] Daniel Cho: That could explain some of the timeouts we saw in our internal stress test.
[03:44] Marco Ruiz: Possibly. We'll instrument more.
[03:46] Lena Park: Let's talk tuning — Marco what knobs did you change and what are the low-effort tweaks we should try?
[03:52] Marco Ruiz: We tried symmetric vs asymmetric quant, per-channel vs per-tensor, and two calibration datasets: 'clinical-short' and 'clinical-long'. Per-channel symmetric quant did best for stability on logits; asymmetric introduced more edge-case drift. Also bias correction after quantization helped on entity precision. For quick wins: 1) use per-channel symmetric INT8 if you must use INT8; 2) enable bias-correction post-quant; 3) set a stricter generation temperature and add a reranker step for entity mentions.
[04:22] Priya Sethi: How much extra latency does the reranker add?
[04:25] Marco Ruiz: Minimal if you do a small candidate rerank (we do top-3 candidates) — about 10-30ms on average depending on your routing. The cost overhead is small compared to a full FP16 pass.
[04:34] Marta Gomez: Are there known kernel patches for A100 to improve INT8 fidelity?
[04:38] Marco Ruiz: There are vendor optimizations and kernel variants; on H100 we used the optimized FP8 kernels which gave better fidelity. A100's INT8 path is mature but can be noisier depending on microcode. We can coordinate with your cloud infra team if you want a vendor-level bench.
[04:52] Lena Park: On cost — what's the cost delta we showed in the sheet?
[04:55] Marco Ruiz: Roughly, INT8 reduces GPU compute cost per token by ~40% because of throughput increase and lower memory pressure, FP8 about 25%. Depending on your unit economics for clinical summarization (you showed ~0.8c per call in FP16) that could shave unit cost to ~0.5c (FP8) or ~0.3-0.4c (INT8) assuming similar request patterns.
[05:15] Daniel Cho: Those per-call numbers are helpful. If we split traffic by risk, we'd get the best of both worlds.
[05:19] Priya Sethi: One more question: did you see any tokenization-related regressions? Sometimes quantization interacts with byte-pair encodings.
[05:26] Marco Ruiz: We intentionally ran identical tokenizers; no BPE-level regressions found but we did see small probability mass shifts on subword boundaries that could change exact token-level generation in rare cases.
[05:40] Lena Park: Good. Now let's capture the specific follow-ups. Aisha, can you drive the security doc ask?
[05:45] Aisha Khan: Yep. I'll send SOC2 and HIPAA packaging and the KMS integration note. We heard the KMS question last week about customer-managed keys for Private deployments — we'll include the RedWood Private KMS integration note and HSM recommendations.
[05:58] Marta Gomez: We also need an explicit audit-log sample for token-level logs retained for 30 days. Is that doable?
[06:03] Aisha Khan: Yes, we'll attach a sample log format and retention options.
[06:08] Speaker 1: Quick nit — we mentioned earlier converting some of our workloads to on-prem; is that more work with the quantized models?
[06:14] Marco Ruiz: On-prem runs generally need our runtime packaging and the same quantized models; the main additional work is around drivers and kernel variants on your HW. We support an on-prem package and will help test the kernel paths.
[06:26] Daniel Cho: About rollout strategies — can Redwood support canaries by model tag and auto-fallback to FP16 if we detect confidence issues?
[06:33] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood can do model routing by tag, and we can wire a fallback policy that watches confidence and error rates. We can provide a recommended canary schedule in the spreadsheet.
[06:43] Priya Sethi: For the hallucination CSV, can you include payload context so we can triage easily?
[06:48] Marco Ruiz: Absolutely — we'll include the exact prompt, model seed, generated output, and FP16 comparison.
[06:55] Lena Park: Timing — Marco, can you run the 24-hour Dedicated run next week?
[06:59] Marco Ruiz: Yes, I'll schedule the FP8 vs INT8 24h run on Dedicated starting Monday, capture p50/p95 and token/sec and memory residency stats. I'll also try the AVX kernel variant on one node so we can compare vendor-specific deltas.
[07:12] Marta Gomez: And if FP8 looks stable over 24h we can push it to canary for the non-sensitive route.
[07:16] Marco Ruiz: Exactly. We'll also add a short script to auto-compare prompt-level metrics and flag any regression >2% on entity precision.
[07:25] Daniel Cho: On pricing — Lena can you send the Dedicated burst pricing and our estimated monthly run cost if we do 20k calls/day?
[07:31] Lena Park: Yup I'll put that in the sheet and include two scenarios: FP8-primary and mixed FP8/INT8 split.
[07:38] Priya Sethi: One last technical note — did you try bias correction after quantization?
[07:42] Marco Ruiz: Yes bias-correction helped recover ~0.8% of the entity precision on INT8 and about 0.2% on FP8. It's a recommended step during quant pipeline.
[07:51] Speaker 1: There was some background noise, sorry.
[07:54] Lena Park: No worries. Okay, quick recap and next steps: Marco runs 24h Dedicated perf run (FP8 & INT8) starting Monday; Priya to share extra hallucination prompts; Lena to share pricing and updated sheet; Aisha to send security docs and KMS note. We'll reconvene in one week same time. Any other blockers?
[08:15] Marta Gomez: None from me. Thanks.
[08:17] Daniel Cho: Thanks everyone.
[08:18] Priya Sethi: Thanks.
[08:19] Marco Ruiz: Thanks all.
[08:20] Lena Park: End call.
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription noise; speakers labeled but one unlabeled sample present. Shared artifact: benchmark sheet link included in transcript.
